name: Nuberu
body:
Nuberu
CR 14

This wild-haired giant has long hair and beard, wearing goat leathers and a big hat, and carrying an oversized axe.

XP 38,400
CN Medium fey (air)
Init +6; Senses darkvision 90 ft., low-light vision; Perception +32

DEFENSE

AC 29, touch 17, flat-footed 22 (+6 Dex, +1 dodge, +12 natural)
hp 209 (22d6+132)
Fort +15, Ref +19, Will +18
Immune charm, electricity, poison; Resist cold 15, fire 15; SR 25

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., fly 80 ft. (good)
Melee +1 anarchic greataxe +20/+15/+10 (1d12+11/×3 plus 2d6 vs. lawful)
Ranged 2 lightning arcs +17 touch (5d6 electricity)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 20th; concentration +24)

At will—shocking grasp
3/day—bestow curse (DC 18), discordant blast, lightning bolt (DC 18)
1/day—chain lightning (DC 21), gaseous form, storm of vengeance (DC 24), stormbolts (DC 23)

STATISTICS

Str 25, Dex 23, Con 22, Int 16, Wis 17, Cha 18
Base Atk +11; CMB +18; CMD 35
Feats Alertness, Dodge, Elemental Focus (electricity), Great Fortitude, Improved Great Fortitude, Improved Iron Will, Iron Will, Mobility, Point-Blank Shot, Shot On The Run, Weapon Focus (greataxe)
Skills Acrobatics +31, Bluff +29, Disguise +29, Fly +35, Knowledge (nature) +28, Perception +32, Sense Motive +32, Spellcraft +25, Stealth +31
Languages Auran, Common, Sylvan
Gear +1 anarchic greataxe

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Lighting Arc (Su)

Nuberu’s lighting arc has a range of 120 feet.

ECOLOGY

Environment any oceans
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

A nuberu represents two sides of the same coin, being both wicked and evil as well as benevolent and helpful.

Believed by some to be demigods—or even a single unique demigod—nuberus represents the danger and raw power of storms, rain, and thunder. Sometimes they are seen wearing dark pelts and traveling in a wolf-pulled chariot. Nuberus often are blamed for destroying crops and homes. Their appearance is also associated with dark skies, shipwrecks, flooding, and damaging lightning strikes. Despite all the harm that is credited to nuberus, he is often called upon by farmers and shepherds to bring rain to their crops and pastures, especially during times of drought.

This duality of the nuberu’s nature makes sense to those who are affected by their actions. They know the nuberu to be unpredictable, bringing both large disasters and great prosperity, depending on his moods. Because of these wild mood swings, wise folk choose carefully whether to approach the nuberu for help, as angering him is likely to bring destruction down on everyone.

Nuberus are believed to make their homes in the mountains and are sometimes depicted as hermits or shepherds. They are known to have a fondness for smoking a pipe, and often enjoy a stiff drink. In many stories from the cultures familiar with him, a nuberu is portrayed as a wise old man who can provide guidance and advice to those who seek it. Also associated with the natural world, they are said to have a deep connection to the animals and plants of the oceans, forests, and mountains.

Despite the positive things he often does for people, nuberus are known for explosive fits of devastation, sometimes destroying an entire village for simple amusement. When shown a lack of respect, a nuberu can become quite vengeful.

Some light candles and ring bells during terrible storms beause they believe it will scare a nuberu away.
